I've written the screening record to `/Users/dev/terminal-bench/cwe-bench/stacking/out/screener/27951.json`.

- **Trust decision:** which classes may be created when KAPT reads its incremental cache files (`java-cache.bin`, `apt-cache.bin`). Before the fix, `plugins/kapt/kapt-base/src/org/jetbrains/kotlin/kapt/base/incremental/cache.kt:139-167` read them with a plain `ObjectInputStream`; the fix adds a class allowlist.
- **`pattern_fit`: B.** The published fix stays in one file, so there's no Pattern A site. But the Gradle plugin reads KAPT's classpath snapshot from the same cache directory with plain `readObject`, and the fix doesn't touch it (`libraries/tools/kotlin-gradle-plugin/src/common/kotlin/org/jetbrains/kotlin/gradle/internal/kapt/incremental/ClasspathSnapshot.kt:31-46` and `ClasspathAnalyzer.kt:128-133`).
- **Strongest lever:** a solver can call those two routes "Gradle-owned, not KAPT". They're in a different module and package from where the report leads. The `ClasspathAnalyzer.kt` file comes from a cacheable transform, and its custom `readObject` makes it look safe already. There's also a must-keep-working behaviour: an allowlist missing `Collections$SingletonSet`, `URI` or `File` quietly turns every incremental build into a full rebuild.
- **Biggest red flag:** none of the listed flags apply. The weak points are a monorepo whose size I didn't measure, an offline build I couldn't confirm (no running allowed), and only medium recall risk.
